name: Arba'a Turub
description: Arba'a Turub (literally Four Packs of Cards) is a massive-scale Somali partnership game that pushes the boundaries of traditional trick-taking. Using a staggering 144-card deck and hands of 36 cards each, it combines the structural logic of Whist with an unusual 'Progressive Win' condition that requires a team to outdo their own previous performance to claim the match.

overview.description: Arba'a Turub (literally Four Packs of Cards) is a massive-scale Somali partnership game that pushes the boundaries of traditional trick-taking. Using a staggering 144-card deck and hands of 36 cards each, it combines the structural logic of Whist with an unusual 'Progressive Win' condition that requires a team to outdo their own previous performance to claim the match.

history.origins: A unique Somali evolution of European Whist, likely developed during periods of colonial influence and adapted to local social settings. Its name 'Arba'a Turub' signifies the four decks required to play.
timeline: 20th Century: Developed as a competitive adult game in Somali urban centers like Mogadishu.
1990s: Documented by historians like Alexey Lobashev through Somali diaspora accounts.
Present: Remains a culturally significant game in East Africa and the Somali diaspora.
history.cultural: Typically played by adults in social clubs. It is known for its physical signalling (knocks and clicks) and intense partnership collaboration.
history.evolution: The game expanded hands from the standard 13 to 36 cards to create a much longer, more endurance-based strategic game.

setup.players: 4 players in two fixed partnerships (North-South vs East-West).
setup.deck: 144 cards. Prepared by taking four 52-card decks and removing all 2s, 3s, 4s, and 5s. Ranks: A(high), K, Q, J, 10, 9, 8, 7, 6(low).
setup.dealing: Deal starts clockwise. Each player receives 36 cards in batches of 3. **Crucial**: After the first 3 cards are dealt to the player on the dealer's left (Eldest Hand), they must declare trumps immediately.
setup.equipment: Four identical decks, table space large enough for 144 cards.

rules.objective: Win two consecutive hands (deals). The second consecutive win must contain more tricks than the first win.
rules.gameplay: 1. **Trump Calling**: Eldest hand calls trumps after seeing only their first three cards. 2. **Trick Play**: Eldest leads. Players MUST follow suit if possible. 3. **Identical Card Rule**: If two or more identical cards are played to one trick, the one played FIRST wins (if it is the highest rank). 4. **Signalling**: Partners are permitted to signal suit strength via knocks (strong) or tongue-clicks (weak). 5. **Match Resolution**: If a team wins a hand, they must win the next hand with a higher trick count to end the match. If they lose the second hand, the count resets. If they win with fewer tricks, it is a draw and they must try again.
keyRules: Large Hands: Managing 36 cards requires physical organization and stamina.
Early Trump: Calling trumps on just 3 cards introduces a massive element of luck and risk-taking.
First-Card Advantage: Since multiple identical cards exist, the lead has a significant advantage in tie-breaking.

strategy.basic: Declare a trump suit you hold even one card of in your first three. Statistically, with 36 cards coming your way, you will likely find more of that suit.
strategy.intermediate: Counting: With 14 packs of each card in play (4 of each suit/rank), you must track how many Aces of Spades have fallen. Once 3 have appeared, the 4th is a 'Bobby' (unbeatable).
strategy.advanced: Signal Coordination: Use the knock/click system to let your partner know if they should 'bleee' (drain) the opponents' trumps or save their high cards for a long-suit run.
tips: Don't waste high cards on small tricks early in the hand. With 36 tricks, the 'endgame' starts much later than in typical Whist.
Remember the identical card rule: playing your Ace of Spades after an opponent has already played one means you CANNOT win the trick with it.

variations.description: A faster version using only 72 cards (two decks).

scoring.description: Scoring is binary (Hand won or Hand lost/drawn).
scoring.winCondition: Progressive Consecutive Wins: Win Hand A (Tricks > 18), then Win Hand B (Tricks > Hand A's count).

synthesis.shortDescription: Somalia's legendary quadruple-deck Whist variant. Challenge yourself with massive hands and a unique progressive win condition where you must beat your own record to win the match.
